summary.text: A conditional expectation is the expected value of a random variable, worked out using its conditional probability distribution.
When the variable can take only a finite number of values, the conditions are that it can take only a subset of those values.
With ten years of daily rainfall, the unconditional expectation averages all the days, while conditioning on March averages only the March days.

facts.label: Other names
facts.value: Conditional expected value, or conditional mean

facts.label: Rainfall record
facts.value: 3652 days over ten years, of which 310 fall in March

facts.label: Narrower condition
facts.value: Conditioning on March 2 averages just ten days

facts.label: Modern definition
facts.value: Generalised in works of Halmos and Doob from 1953

items.prompt: A weather station has rainfall for every day of ten years. You want the expected rainfall for a day you know falls in March. What do you average?

options.label: Every day in the whole ten-year record
Only the March days in the record
Only the rainiest days in the record
Only the most recent March in the record

items.explain: Knowing the day is in March is the condition, so you average the rainfall over the days of the record that fall in March.

items.prompt: Using that same ten-year rainfall record, you know nothing about tomorrow's date. Which number is the expected rainfall?

options.label: The average rainfall over all the days in the record
The average over just the wettest month
The rainfall on the last day of the record
The average over only the days in one season

items.explain: With no condition, the unconditional expectation is the average across all the days of the record.

items.prompt: In a ten-year daily rainfall record, you condition on the date being March 2. How many days does that average cover?

options.label: 310 days
3652 days
10 days
1 day

items.explain: Each year has one March 2, so the average covers the ten days with that specific date.

items.prompt: A die can show six values. You are told the roll is even. What does that condition do to the values being considered?

options.label: It restricts them to a subset of the possible values
It adds new values the die could not show
It makes every value equally likely again
It removes all the randomness from the roll

items.explain: For a variable with finitely many values, the conditions mean it can only take a subset of those values.

items.prompt: Someone works out an average using the probabilities that hold once a certain condition is known, instead of the original probabilities. What have they found?

options.label: An unconditional expectation
A marginal distribution
A conditional expectation
A joint distribution

items.explain: A conditional expectation is an expected value evaluated with respect to the conditional probability distribution.

items.prompt: Why do statisticians and applied mathematicians often use approximations of conditional expectation?

options.label: It is undefined whenever a variable takes finitely many values
Working it out exactly can be difficult
Approximations are always more accurate
It can only be defined for rainfall data

items.explain: Because it is hard to calculate analytically, it is often approximated in applied work.
